description: We are team Straw-hats, taking on the Space Mission Design Game challenge! We're building an engaging, realistic space mission simulation. Whether you're a developer, UI/UX designer, game creator, or space enthusiast, we’d love to have you onboard. Let’s collaborate, innovate, and build an awesome project together!
summary: MoonLander is a free, browser-based 3D space mission game where players design, launch and operate a complete mission, from science goal to spacecraft, orbit, launch vehicle and live operations. Every choice has a consequence: a bigger instrument adds science but also mass, power draw, data volume and cost, so players learn mission design by feeling the trade-offs instead of reading about them. A built-in Space Academy, a coaching assistant and plain-language tooltips let a complete beginner play, while an engineering-grade simulation keeps experts challenged. Scenarios are based on real NASA missions, such as Landsat, TESS, DSCOVR, LRO and Europa Clipper, and use NASA data: planetary positions, exoplanet catalogues and real solar-storm events. A causal debrief explains why a mission succeeded or failed and offers a one-click what-if. It addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by making the whole mission system tangible and teaching the engineering decisions behind real missions, which helps build the next generation of space engineers.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

MoonLander turns the NASA mission-design process into a playable game. Players pick a science objective, set requirements, build a spacecraft (structure, power, communications, computer, attitude control, propulsion, thermal and instruments), choose an orbit and launch vehicle, then fly the mission in a live 3D simulation. Mass, power, budget, data, communications, time and risk are tracked on a live dashboard, and a Mission Advisor explains every warning in plain language with a one-click fix. A launch-compatibility check blocks designs that are too heavy for the chosen rocket and orbit. After the mission, a debrief ranks the decisions that mattered most, shows what would have changed with a different choice, and matches the player's design to a real NASA mission.

HOW IT WORKS

A deterministic physics engine runs behind every gauge. It uses orbital period and eclipse geometry, the rocket equation for fuel, solar-array and battery power budgets, ground-station pass geometry for data downlink, radiation dose, and a cost and schedule model. Interplanetary missions use patched-conic transfers, launch windows and a Lambert solver. The simulation is seeded, so the same design always produces the same result and any mission can be replayed and shared.

EDUCATION FIRST

The game assumes no prior knowledge. A Space Academy teaches orbits, power, communications and rockets through interactive lessons. A coaching assistant guides each step, every control has a tooltip, and a plain-language mode swaps jargon for analogies. Players can ask the game to suggest or auto-build a valid design, and it explains every choice it makes. A story campaign casts the player as a new Mission Director, so decisions carry consequences across chapters. Pilot profiles, mission history and achievements reward good engineering and encourage replay. [Add crew mode only if it is live: Up to four players can work together in distinct roles.]

NASA DATA AND RESOURCES

The game uses the JPL approximate planetary orbital elements, the NASA Exoplanet Archive, NASA DONKI space-weather events, and NASA planetary fact sheets and mission pages for spacecraft and mission parameters. Its structure follows NASA's Design and Develop Science Missions guidance, Concept Maturity Levels and the Mission Design Lab approach. All values used in the game are simplified and clearly labelled as approximate.

TOOLS

Next.js, React and TypeScript for the app; react-three-fiber and Three.js for 3D; Zustand for state; Zod for data validation; Vitest and Playwright for testing; GitHub Actions for CI; and Vercel for free hosting. [Add: Supabase for accounts and multiplayer, only if used.]

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It treats mission design as a whole system instead of separate topics, with live cause-and-effect for every decision. The debrief explains why outcomes happened and lets players test a fix. Original story missions and procedurally generated mission patches make each flight feel personal.

IMPACT

MoonLander lets students and curious people experience the trade-offs real mission teams face, and it can be played free in any browser with no sign-in. It is designed so new missions, planets and scenarios can be added as data, which makes it easy for educators and the community to extend.
